verdict.rationale: Granola documents an official MCP server that connects Claude, ChatGPT and other AI tools to meeting notes, with search across notes and transcripts, so the core of the story is first-party. The MCP docs in the evidence do not mention OAuth authentication or action-item retrieval; action items appear only in the separate REST API docs, so story coverage is incomplete. Missing for 10: documented OAuth auth flow for the MCP connection, action-item querying via MCP, a list of the MCP tools exposed, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an official MCP server lets Claude or any MCP client query my meetings — search, transcripts, action items — with OAuth, no glue code

citations.quote: Connect Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI tools to your Granola meeting notes via MCP. Query your notes, search transcripts, and get meeting insights in your favorite AI assistants.
Once connected you can use this to: search through your meeting notes, find specific topics discussed in past meetings
